explain.say: Think of a burger. Bun on top, tasty fillings in the middle, bun at the bottom. A good essay is built the same way! Look at the board. The top bun is your introduction: a hook to grab the reader, then your main answer to the question.

explain.say: Your main answer is called a thesis, one sentence that says what you will argue. For example: School uniforms help students focus. Everything in the essay backs it up. What would your thesis be about homework?

explain.say: Now look at the fillings: the body paragraphs. Each one makes one point, gives evidence like a fact or a quote, then explains how it proves your thesis. Point, evidence, explain. Can you think of one point for your homework essay?

explain.say: See the next two layers? More body paragraphs, each with a new point. Start each one with a topic sentence and link back to your question. Three strong points usually work well. What could your second point be?

explain.say: The bottom bun is the conclusion. Sum up your points and answer the question again in fresh words, with no new ideas. Brilliant, you can build an essay! Challenge: plan a burger essay on whether every child should learn to swim.

faq.q: How do I structure an essay?
faq.a: Use an introduction with your thesis, then body paragraphs that each make one point with evidence, then a conclusion that sums up and answers the question.

faq.q: What goes in an essay introduction?
faq.a: A hook to catch interest, a little background, and your thesis: one clear sentence that answers the question.
asks: How do I start an essay?

faq.q: How do I write a conclusion?
faq.a: Sum up your main points, restate your answer in new words, and end with a final thought. Do not add new evidence.
asks: How do I end an essay?

faq.a: A thesis statement is one sentence, usually at the end of the introduction, that states the main argument of your essay.
It stands for Point, Evidence, Explain, and sometimes Link. It is a way to build each body paragraph.

facts: The word essay comes from the French essai, meaning an attempt or a try.
The French writer Michel de Montaigne made the essay popular with his Essais in 1580.
